subject.title: Feature: Subscribe to WhatsApp call events (Baileys)

question: What privacy and exposure boundary should the WhatsApp plugin use for inbound Baileys call events before implementation?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but call metadata includes sensitive contact/activity information and the repository policy treats new config, plugin hooks, and security boundaries as maintainer decisions rather than automatic repair work.

options.title: Opt-in sanitized WhatsApp event surface
options.body: Add a default-off WhatsApp-owned call-event path that normalizes minimal metadata, applies existing inbound access-control gates, and exposes it only through a documented hook/session/tool contract.

options.title: Defer until a broader activity API exists
options.body: Keep this issue open but wait for a generic channel activity/event contract so calls, reactions, and similar non-message events do not grow separate one-off APIs.

options.title: Reject call tracking for privacy
options.body: Close the request as not planned if OpenClaw should avoid tracking WhatsApp call metadata even when Baileys exposes the event.

recommendation.title: Opt-in sanitized WhatsApp event surface
recommendation.body: Add a default-off WhatsApp-owned call-event path that normalizes minimal metadata, applies existing inbound access-control gates, and exposes it only through a documented hook/session/tool contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the adjacent WhatsApp call surface and already provided the strongest issue-scoping comment for this inbound-call boundary.
